title: Tracy shutown ordering causes many stringnames in exit report.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible since the introduction of Automatic GDScript profiling of because of the StringName internment.
So that's ~4.6+


### System information

Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - AMD Ryzen 7 6800HS Creator Edition (16 threads) - 13.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

On closure Godot reports too many unclaimed StringNames.
Some of those StringNames I noticed were created by the Tracy profiling macros I was using while working on cleaning up the GDScript instrumentation, and working on more features.
It is because the order of cleanup is incorrect.

1. StringName::cleanup() is called in the unregister_core_types() method called from Main::cleanup()
2. godot_cleanup_profiler() is called in a platform specific way just before quitting the application.

Because the StringNames are interned, the StringName::cleanup() reports all of the names held by the internment.

In my local fork I have experimented with moving the profiling cleanup to Main::cleanup() just before the unregister_core_types() and have not experienced a crash as a temporary fix. But I think more care is needed in a real solution.



### Steps to reproduce

Run any (debug?) version with Tracy compiled in with --verbose to get the stringname report.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

1. Compile Godot with Tracy profiling enabled
2. Run godot with --verbose
3. Check the stringname report on finish
